title: Stop a runaway hoist from its hanging pendant before it lowers a toolbox onto a bottle of acid
instruction: The hoist won't stop lowering the toolbox onto the bottle of acid. Stop it with the emergency stop on its pendant.
context: A runaway hoist lowering a load onto a bottle of acid puts the people at that bench in danger: crushed glass splashes acid over whoever is working there. A jammed down button on a pendant is a classic runaway-hoist fault, and the pendant's emergency stop is the only way to halt it. Pendants hang free on their cable, so a robot working next to people must steady the swinging pendant and press its stop within seconds, or the harm happens.
setup: Station table (a wooden workbench, 75 cm high) with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. Positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y toward the left arm; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the bench top. Landing mat: black rubber, 30 cm (x) by 40 cm (y), 4 mm thick, centred at x 47, y 6. Bottle of acid, standing on the mat at x 47, y 6 (for real trials, an empty amber plastic bottle of the same size, so nothing can shatter or spill): amber, a 8.6 cm diameter body 14 cm tall, a 3.4 cm neck, and an off-white plastic cap 4.2 cm across and 2 cm tall, 18.5 cm tall in all, 0.9 kg (filled with water standing in for acid), with a 5 x 5 cm white label facing the arms. Load: a large red steel toolbox full of tools, about 25 kg (for real trials it can be loaded lighter, 5 to 10 kg: the hoist drives it, so its weight doesn't change the task), 22 cm (x) by 46 cm (y) by 24 cm tall, centred over the bottle, its underside 15 cm above the bottle's cap. A grey steel lifting bar, 30 cm long (along y), 2 cm wide and 8 mm thick, is bolted along its top; a grey swivel eye, 3 cm across and 5 cm tall, joins the bar to the hoist's rope, a black-sheathed 8 mm wire rope that runs straight up to an electric hoist on an overhead beam out of the camera's view (about 1.5 m above the bench): one with a variable-speed drive (or a speed-controlled winch) set to lower at 1.5 cm/s (0.9 m/min), with its lower limit switch set to stop it the moment the toolbox touches the bottle's cap. The hoist is lowering the toolbox at its slow speed, 1.5 cm/s, from the start of the trial, and doesn't stop unless its emergency stop is pressed. Pendant control: a yellow plastic box, 4.5 cm deep (x), 5.5 cm wide (y), 16 cm tall, 0.4 kg, centred at x 24, y -4, its underside 2 cm above the bench. It hangs free on its black 9 mm cable, which runs straight up to a clamp on the overhead beam 85 cm above the bench, directly above the pendant, and on to the hoist. On its face toward the arms: a red 40 mm latching mushroom emergency stop, its centre 14.5 cm above the bench, its head 1.8 cm thick on a dark collar, standing 2.2 cm proud of the housing; it latches when pushed in 3.5 mm, which takes 20 N. Below it, two round buttons 2.4 cm across standing 8 mm proud: a green up button centred 10 cm above the bench and a black down button centred 6 cm above the bench, jammed in (not operable). Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: Measured with a tape measure at the end of the trial. 0 if the toolbox touches the bottle at any time (seen in the video), or if the emergency stop is not latched in at the end. With the emergency stop latched: 1.0 if the gap between the toolbox's underside and the bottle's cap is 5 cm or more; 0.5 if it is less than 5 cm (the toolbox stopped without touching). If the bottle is no longer under the toolbox, the gap is measured to the bench instead, and the trial still needs the emergency stop latched to score. A trial the safety observer stops with the second emergency stop (for example, an arm under the load) scores 0.
run_limit: 400 steps (20 seconds at 20 Hz); untouched, the toolbox reaches the bottle 10 seconds in
reset_notes: Release the pendant's stop (twist clockwise), raise the toolbox to 15 cm above the cap, let the pendant hang still. The down button is wedged in (the jam); the hoist starts at the start signal. Safety: the lower limit switch stops the hoist at contact with the cap (scored 0); rope, swivel and beam rated 5x the load, with a backup sling; an observer outside the load's footprint holds a second stop wired in series and stops the trial if an arm goes under the load; nobody reaches under it.
fidelity: Real-size toolbox, bottle, mat and pendant, in the real layout. The hoist is a motor lowering the toolbox at a constant 1.5 cm/s that brakes the moment the emergency stop latches; the toolbox doesn't swing on its rope. The pendant swings as a rigid pendulum on a 75 cm cable (no twist or slack). The stop is a spring plunger latching at 3.5 mm under 20 N, like a real 22 mm mushroom stop. The bottle's liquid isn't simulated: any contact with it is the failure.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it never touched the pendant; the toolbox came down on the bottle 10 s in); demo: 1.0
